articles.title: India's SIP Machine Has Grown Tenfold in a Decade. Equity Mutual Fund Flows Just Hit a One-Year Low. What NRIs Should Read Into Both.
articles.excerpt: Monthly SIP contributions surged from ₹3,189 crore to ₹30,954 crore in ten years even as foreign investors dumped a record $30 billion of Indian stocks in 2026.
articles.image_caption: Stock market trading screens displaying financial data and market movements
articles.nri_angle: NRIs deciding whether to stay invested in India face a structural shift: domestic SIP-driven capital now provides floor support that makes timing the market from abroad harder, while FCNR deposits offer a complementary low-risk dollar yield.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Have Fled 43 of India's 50 Biggest Stocks. Domestic Money Is Filling the Void.
articles.excerpt: FII ownership in Indian equities has plunged to a 14-year low of 14.7 per cent, while domestic institutional holdings have surged to a record 18.9 per cent — a structural shift that reshapes risk and opportunity for NRI investors.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai — foreign institutional investors have pulled back from most of India's top 50 stocks
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors face a double bind: the record foreign exit from Indian equities has eroded returns in dollar terms, but the structural shift toward domestic ownership may reduce future volatility and create a more favourable entry point.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s IT Stocks Have Lost 27 Per Cent This Year. For NRI Tech Workers, the Pain Is Doubly Personal.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has shed more than a quarter of its value in 2026 as AI disruption fears collide with macro headwinds. For the millions of Indian-origin professionals who work in the same industry they invest in, the exposure is uniquely concentrated.
articles.image_caption: A stock market trading screen displaying real-time financial data and price movements
articles.nri_angle: NRI tech workers often hold ESOPs in Indian IT firms, invest in IT-heavy mutual funds, and work in the very sector AI threatens to disrupt — creating a rare triple concentration of career, portfolio, and identity risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GIFT City Just Got Its First US Company Listing. Here Is What NRIs Need to Know.
articles.excerpt: Banking assets at $111 billion, US stocks now accessible, and the first American IPO on Indian exchanges — India's answer to Dubai and Singapore is crossing a threshold.
articles.image_caption: GIFT One tower in Gujarat — the centrepiece of India's first International Financial Services Centre
articles.nri_angle: GIFT City is positioning itself as a tax-efficient hub specifically for NRI wealth management, cross-border investing, and India-linked portfolios — a direct alternative to routing capital through Dubai or Singapore.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Opened Its Stock Market to Every Foreigner on Earth. Here Is What Changed Overnight.
articles.excerpt: A sweeping FEMA amendment notified on June 12 replaces the NRI-only investment framework with one that lets any individual residing outside India buy and sell listed Indian equities — a historic shift in capital account liberalisation.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs already invested in Indian equities now share the playing field with every foreign individual globally — understanding the new rules, limits, and safeguards is essential to protect existing holdings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits. Here Is How to Get the Best Rate Before September.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's unprecedented forex swap has sparked a rate war among banks. Emkay calculates leveraged returns could reach 22%. The window closes September 30.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn 6-7% on dollar deposits at Indian banks with zero currency risk before the RBI's concessional swap window closes September 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. For NRI Investors, the Timing Could Not Be Better.
articles.excerpt: Tax exemptions, subsidised hedging, and a $3 billion corporate debt rush — India's most aggressive capital-market reforms in years are rewriting the playbook for overseas fixed-income investors, with Bloomberg index inclusion now weeks away from a decision.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building, headquarters of the central bank driving India's bond-market reforms
articles.nri_angle: NRI depositors benefit directly from RBI's fully subsidised hedging on foreign currency deposits, while the tax exemptions on government bonds make Indian fixed income a viable portfolio allocation for the first time in years — particularly for diaspora investors burned by the rupee's depreciation and looking for yield with policy support.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: El Nino Is Officially Here. India's Monsoon, Food Prices, and NRI Portfolios Are All in the Firing Line.
articles.excerpt: The US Climate Prediction Center and India's Met department have both confirmed moderate-to-strong El Nino conditions during the monsoon season — the first since 2023 and potentially one of the strongest on record. Here is what it means for your money.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian equity, bond, or commodity exposure face direct portfolio risk from El Nino through FMCG margin compression, rupee weakness, and potential RBI policy shifts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BlackRock and Lighthouse Canton Say India Has Been 'Over-Punished.' The Contrarian Case for NRI Investors Is Getting Louder.
articles.excerpt: After a record 30 billion dollars in foreign outflows, the world's largest asset manager and a major wealth firm argue that India's lack of a direct AI play is an advantage — not a liability — and that the worst of the selloff may be over.
articles.image_caption: A stock market trading screen displaying financial data and price movements
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who paused SIPs or sold India positions during the record $30 billion outflow are now hearing from BlackRock and Lighthouse Canton that the selloff has gone too far — a signal that could reshape diaspora portfolio decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vedanta Splits Into Five: Four Demerged Companies Hit the Stock Market on Monday. Here Is What NRI Investors Need to Know.
articles.excerpt: The largest corporate demerger in Indian history reaches its final act as Vedanta Aluminium, Vedanta Oil & Gas, Vedanta Power, and Vedanta Iron & Steel begin trading on the BSE and NSE on June 15 — creating pure-play bets on India's commodity future.
articles.image_caption: Anil Agarwal, founder and chairman of Vedanta Resources, whose demerger creates four new listed companies on Monday (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs holding Vedanta shares through demat or overseas broker accounts will find four new stocks in their portfolios on Monday — understanding the listing mechanics, trade restrictions, and tax implications is essential before the first trade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US-Iran Peace Deal Hopes Send Nifty Soaring 2%: What the Oil Shock Reversal Means for Indian Markets and NRI Portfolios
articles.excerpt: A surprise memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran triggered the biggest single-day rally in months, with crude prices tumbling and Indian equities surging across sectors
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai — Indian equities surged on US-Iran peace deal hopes
articles.nri_angle: NRI investment portfolios, oil price impact on Indian economy, forex and remittance implications
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Gold Tariff Gamble: A 15% Import Duty, a $14 Billion Smuggling Surge, and the NRI Caught in Between
articles.excerpt: New Delhi's bid to curb gold demand and protect forex reserves has revived grey-market channels that could move over 100 tonnes this year.
articles.image_caption: Gold remains culturally central to Indian weddings and festivals, making tariff hikes a deeply personal issue for the diaspora.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who regularly send gold home for weddings and festivals, the tariff hike means higher costs, more scrutiny at customs, and a growing temptation to use grey-market channels — with serious legal consequences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nifty Surges Nearly 2% on Iran Peace Hopes as RBI Opens a Dollar Goldmine for NRI Depositors
articles.excerpt: Indian markets posted their best single-day gain in two months as oil prices collapsed on US-Iran deal optimism — and the RBI's subsidised hedging programme is making NRI dollar deposits the most attractive they have been in years
articles.image_caption: A stock market display showing real-time financial data — the Nifty 50 posted its best day in two months on Iran peace hopes
articles.nri_angle: Banks are offering NRIs 6-7% on dollar FCNR deposits with RBI-subsidised hedging — a rare window that closes in September; diaspora investors should evaluate before the deadline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Opens Insurance to 100% Foreign Ownership — What NRIs Need to Know
articles.excerpt: The landmark reform allows global insurers to fully own Indian companies, promising better products for the diaspora and reshaping a $143 billion market
articles.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman — India has opened its insurance sector to 100% foreign ownership (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs stand to gain from cross-border insurance products, easier policy servicing, and new investment opportunities as global insurers enter India with full ownership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Braces for a Wider Fiscal Deficit as Iran War Costs Mount and the Fed Signals No Relief
articles.excerpt: New Delhi may let the deficit hit 4.8% of GDP to absorb energy subsidies, even as US inflation surges to 4.2% and the rupee tests new lows — but a potential Iran deal could change everything.
articles.image_caption: Indian currency notes — the rupee has fallen to 95.68 against the dollar as foreign investors pull record capital from Indian markets.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending remittances are benefiting from a weaker rupee, but those with Indian investments face a double hit from falling equity markets and currency depreciation — making asset allocation decisions more urgent than ever.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's $315-Billion IT Empire Faces Its AI Reckoning
articles.excerpt: TCS chairman says AI agents will match headcount. Nifty IT is down 25%. And the outsourcing model that built India's middle class is being rewritten in real time
articles.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services, India's largest IT company, where chairman N. Chandrasekaran announced AI agents will soon match the firm's 600,000 employees
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant positions in Indian IT stocks; the sector's 25% decline represents billions in diaspora wealth erosion. The structural shift affects the economic trajectory of young Indians who viewed software engineering as their path to prosperity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Abolished All Taxes on Foreign Bond Investment. One Billion Dollars Flowed In Within Three Days.
articles.excerpt: The tax exemption and expanded market access are designed to lure back foreign capital and lock in a spot in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index. Here is what it means for NRI investors.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors stand to benefit directly from expanded access to Indian government bonds and the removal of tax barriers — the reforms also strengthen the case for FCNR deposits and may stabilise the rupee that has hit their remittance calculations hard this year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
